reviews.checked: Opened all 47 line references in notes/sources/2026-11-14-ui-sdk.md (25 core:, 7 web:, 15 agents:) with surrounding lines; grepped all ten docs files for each of the 11 "not said" items; counted the component list in all five framework files (55 each, identical, claim holds); compared every size figure with raw/2026-11-14-ui-sdk-size.txt and re-ran measure-ui-sdk-size.py (byte-for-byte identical; all imports are static, so no lazy-chunk inflation); verified the ten checksums; re-fetched the npm registry record for @ui-sdk/core and the five adapters, the GitHub repo API, README.md and SECURITY.md at 07:33 UTC 15 Nov 2026. Dates, versions' publish days, Apache-2.0, one listed maintainer, zero runtime dependencies, repo created 26 Oct, 107 open issues, the README beta quote, the Vercel security address, the budget figures and the core:499 contradiction all check out. No blocker found; six major and seven minor corrections follow.

findings.where: "Any time-of-day or appointment-slot helper: dates only." (line 59)
findings.problem: Refuted. The docs list a Time Input component in every framework and document a booking-slot behaviour with overlap checking. The reader's 'not found' was scoped to the Utilities range (core lines 2110-3766) and was generalised to the whole docs. D-013 item 2 names only date picker and calendar for appointment booking, so the appointment-booking scope is understated.
findings.evidence: docs_web-components_llms.txt:1347 "- [Time Input](/docs/web-components/components/time-input): Type a time one part at a time, on the clock your user's language uses." (same entry at react:1613, vue:1339, svelte:1307, solid:1375). docs_core_llms.txt:5208 "### Bookings on a Timeline"; core:5210 "For room bookings, those units can be minutes from midnight."; core:5234 "Values snap to half hours, and bookings can't overlap."; core:5277 "`isSpanFree(bookings, proposed)` checks whether a proposed booking overlaps another on its track." Readers JSON: reader 5 fact 31 and reader 2 fact 28 ("Timeline spans (relevant to appointment booking)") already recorded both.
findings.fix: Delete the bullet. Add under 'Facts that help us': a Time Input component is listed (its page was not read), and core has `createSpans` / `isSpanFree` for time ranges on tracks with snapping and overlap rules (core:5208-5277); focusability and names are left to the author (core:5236). Say what is actually absent: no time-zone-aware date-time value and no ready-made slot picker component.

findings.where: "Any validation message or error-summary pattern." (line 56) and "Toast is the only feedback component" (line 53)
findings.problem: The docs do document a per-field validation message part and a pattern for showing a server's rejection message. The bullet contradicts its own second sentence, which cites that part. Progress is also a listed status component. DECISIONS.md A-16 item 1 repeats this to the CEO as "UI SDK has nothing for two of them (inline feedback and the cost summary)"; that is only true of page-level alerts and error summaries, not of field-level inline feedback.
findings.evidence: docs_web-components_llms.txt:952 "### Label and Validate a Field"; :954 "`ui-field` finds the control inside it and connects the label, description, and error"; :968 "<ui-field-error></ui-field-error>"; :978 "Set the field's `invalid` property to `true` and show the server's message."; Field list entry "Connect a form control to its label, description, and validation errors."; :1335 "[Progress]...: Show a task's progress, or an indeterminate state while its progress is unknown." Reader 5 facts 22 and 24 recorded the field error part.
findings.fix: Reword line 56 to: "Any error-summary pattern. Field has a per-field error part (`ui-field-error`) that shows the browser's message when empty and a server message set by script (web:954, web:978, web:1017)." Reword line 53 to: "No inline alert, page-level status message or error summary. Feedback parts that exist: the field error part, Progress, and Toast, which needs a script call (web:715)." Then correct A-16 item 1 to say UI SDK has nothing for page-level inline feedback and the cost summary.

findings.where: "Password, card and one-time-code fields are hidden from the agent automatically (`agents:1002`)." (line 29)
findings.problem: Stronger than the source. The source says these fields are treated as secret, not hidden. In these docs 'hidden' and 'secret' are two different marks: a secret field stays visible to the agent with its value redacted, and the agent can still type into it. This matters for the checkout EXPLORE item in D-013 item 4 (an agent can type into a card field).
findings.evidence: docs_agents_llms.txt:1002 "Password, card and one-time-code fields are treated as secret without a mark. A hidden input is left out without one." docs_agents_llms.txt:988-989 "| `data-agent-hidden` | Nothing. Components inside are left out of `snapshot` and `query`..." / "| `data-agent-secret` | The component, with its value shown as `"[redacted]"` once it's filled. The agent can still type into it."
findings.fix: Replace with: "The values of password, card and one-time-code fields are redacted from the agent automatically; the agent still sees the field and can type into it (`agents:989`, `agents:1002`). To keep a field from the agent entirely it must be marked `data-agent-hidden`." Move the 'can still type into it' half to 'Facts that cost us'.

findings.where: "**One account publishes it.** The only maintainer listed on the registry is one personal account" (line 37)
findings.problem: The second sentence is true (one maintainer listed), but the heading is not: the two most recent versions of all six packages were published by GitHub Actions through npm trusted publishing, with provenance attestations, not by the personal account. The registry reader recorded this (reader 6, fact 10) and the note dropped it. DECISIONS.md A-16 carries the same wording as a risk: "one publishing account".
findings.evidence: curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@ui-sdk%2fcore (07:33 UTC 15 Nov 2026): versions["0.1.0-beta.3"]._npmUser = {"name": "GitHub Actions", "email": "npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com", "trustedPublisher": {"id": "github", ...}}; dist.attestations.provenance.predicateType = "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1". Same for 0.1.0-beta.2 and for react, vue, svelte, solid, web. Only 0.0.0-stage and 0.1.0-beta.1 were published by the maintainer account. maintainers array length is 1.
findings.fix: Retitle: "One account controls it on the registry." Body: "The only maintainer listed is one personal account. Beta.1 was published from that account; beta.2 and beta.3 were published by the repository's GitHub Actions workflow with provenance attestations (lead re-checked)." Change A-16's risk to "one registry maintainer account".

findings.where: "**Server markup carries state.** Parts render their attributes into the server's HTML (`core:867`)." (line 25)
findings.problem: Stronger than the source for web components, which is the adapter A-16 item 3 takes by default. The cited line's next sentence, and web:1038, say that with web components the author sends the markup and writes the initial ARIA state by hand; nothing computes it on the server. The components reader marked this as conflicting with the no-JavaScript budget.
findings.evidence: docs_core_llms.txt:867 "...On web components, you send the markup and the element connects its behavior once its module loads." docs_web-components_llms.txt:1038 "Plain server-rendered HTML does not calculate the primitive's ARIA state. Here, `aria-pressed="true"` describes the initial button before upgrade and matches `default-pressed`." Reader 5 fact (line 1038): effect "conflicts".
findings.fix: Reword: "With the React, Vue, Svelte and Solid adapters, parts render their attributes into the server's HTML (`core:867`). With web components they do not: we write the initial markup and ARIA state by hand and the element takes over when its script loads (`web:1038`)." List the web-components half under 'Facts that cost us'.

findings.where: "**What was read:** the site's ten text files for agents" (line 9) and the 'What was not read' list (line 12)
findings.problem: The reader record shows no reader was given the Vue, Svelte or Solid files, and the React file was used only to compare its component list. That is about 273 of the 920 kilobytes. findings.evidence: raw/2026-11-14-ui-sdk-and-skills-readers.json: reader sections are core 1-2109 + guides, core 2110-3766, core 3767-5986, core 5987-8084, agents + llms.txt, and "docs_web-components_llms.txt lines 1-1583, web.md lines 1-1572 plus component-list comparison against docs_react_llms.txt". findings.where: "The optional `web.css` gives every component a default look (`web:16`)" (line 40)
findings.problem: Wrong file. The sentence is at web.md line 16, not docs_web-components_llms.txt line 16, and the legend on line 14 defines no prefix for web.md. The fact itself is supported.
findings.evidence: web.md:16 "`web.css` gives every component its default look." docs_web-components_llms.txt:16 "Import the components you need to register their tags, add them to your page, and style them with your own CSS." Reader 5's fact names file web.md, line 16.
findings.fix: Cite as `web.md:16` and add to the legend: "`web.md:` is the no-build Web Components file."

findings.where: "or reduced motion beyond a rule the author writes" (line 57)
findings.problem: The docs do say the library itself responds to the reduced-motion preference in at least one behaviour, and state the outcome for transitions. Two readers recorded these facts. The author-written rule is true only of the panel and entry/exit CSS (core:6230, core:6299).
findings.evidence: docs_core_llms.txt:5913 "With reduced motion, the wheel jumps to an option instead of gliding there." docs_core_llms.txt:6180 "Someone who prefers reduced motion gets the end at once." docs_core_llms.txt:6299 "Add a reduced-motion rule to your CSS, as in the panel example."
findings.fix: Reword: "No general reduced-motion setting. The scroll wheel jumps instead of gliding under reduced motion (`core:5913`); for CSS transitions the author writes the rule (`core:6299`)."

findings.where: "only the Gregorian calendar is supported (`core:2752`)" (line 42)
findings.problem: Slightly stronger than the source, which says the month grid is Gregorian and that calendars sharing Gregorian months keep their own years.
findings.evidence: docs_core_llms.txt:2752 "They keep month and day labels aligned with the Gregorian grid. A locale that uses different months, such as Persian, uses Gregorian labels; calendars that share those months, such as Thai Buddhist, can keep their own years."
findings.fix: "Month grids are Gregorian only: a locale with different months, such as Persian, gets Gregorian labels; one that shares the months, such as Thai Buddhist, keeps its own years (`core:2752`)."

findings.where: "**Announcements default to English** (`core:4472`)" (line 42)
findings.problem: The cited line is one option of one behaviour (the selection rectangle). The general statement is broader than the line. It is supported for eleven behaviour options, each of which the author can override; text passed to `announce()` is the author's own. None of the eleven is a checkout part. A-16 repeats the general form as a risk.
findings.evidence: docs_core_llms.txt:4472 "`message?` ... What screen readers hear when the rectangle lifts. Defaults to English." The same phrase "Defaults to English" appears at core:4482, 4833, 4842, 4854, 5384, 5398, 5446, 5456, 7671, 7680, all on a `message?` option.
findings.fix: "The built-in screen-reader messages of eleven drag, selection and canvas behaviours default to English; each takes a `message` function to replace them (`core:4472` and ten more)."

findings.where: "or any statement on removing unused code when bundling" (line 52)
findings.problem: One such statement exists, in a file no reader was given. The package metadata also declares the bundler hint, which bears on the unmeasured 'an app that bundles the packages may ship less' sentence. The rest of the bullet holds: no size figure from the project (grep for kB, bytes, gzip, tree-shak, sideEffects in the docs returns nothing).
findings.evidence: docs_vue_llms.txt:86 "Each one is still imported from its own entry, so a page bundles only what it uses." Registry: versions["0.1.0-beta.3"].sideEffects = ["*.css"] for @ui-sdk/core.
findings.fix: "No size figure from the project. On bundling, the docs say only that each component is imported from its own entry, so a page bundles only what it uses (Vue file, line 86); the package declares `sideEffects: ["*.css"]`."

findings.where: "231 of the 232 quotes from the docs files were found at the stated line; the one miss is a quote where the reader corrected a typo in the source" (line 11)
findings.problem: Three small inaccuracies. (a) The direction is reversed: the source is correct and the reader's quote has the typo. reviews.checked: Read in full: DECISIONS.md (D-013, A-16, A-17, A-13, A-14, D-008, A-04, A-08), notes/sources/2026-11-14-ui-sdk.md and 2026-11-14-ceo-skills.md, charter/budget.md, principles.md, operating-model.md, checkout-slice.md, benchmark.md, survey.md, vision.md, notes/survey/behaviour-and-distribution.md, PROGRESS.md, scorecard.md, the size measurement, the git log and the uncommitted diff; spot-checked about a dozen lines of the fetched UI SDK docs. All eight questions are answered: 1 one blocker (principle 6) plus budget, decision-right and native-first conflicts; 2 the principle 6 delta and a benchmark row are changed unsaid, and D-013 point 4 lacks an expiry; 3 none of the three A-16 defaults is the most reversible; 4 "What does not change" is narrower than the charter in two places and no written naming convention conflicts with data-slot; 5 "only library found" rests on a survey of three; 6 the A-13 outcome meets the three elements Gate 2 criterion 2 names, but "done" for item 2.1 is not justified; 7 the argument against is fair but not the strongest; 8 item 3.5 cannot decide A-16 point 1 and its tier is too low for the build half.

findings.where: D-013 point 2 "A Souvenir component wraps the UI SDK part ... The version is pinned exactly"; D-013 "Principle: 6, built to last (hence the pin and the wrapper)"; A-16 point 2 "Default taken: accepted"
findings.problem: Q1, Q2, Q3. UI SDK is 0.1.0-beta.3. Putting it inside Souvenir components makes it a pre-release dependency of brick, which principle 6 forbids and the budget sets at a delta of zero. Neither entry mentions the rule; D-013 cites principle 6 as support. No exception list exists, and nothing says who may write one. CLAUDE.md requires the CEO to be asked before a principle's delta changes. A-16 point 2 asks about "accepting a beta" without saying it overrides a charter rule, and takes the less reversible default.
findings.evidence: charter/principles.md:135 "Nothing in brick depends on software with a pre-release version tag or a version below 1.0 (*[starting value]*), except items on a written exception list." charter/budget.md:97 "Zero pre-release dependencies in brick." charter/principles.md:28 "Nor are the other checks of principles 5 to 7 that block a change: a pre-release dependency". CLAUDE.md: "Ask me first, under 'Awaiting CEO': changes to the principles or their deltas". `grep -rn -i "exception list" --include=*.md .` returns only charter/principles.md:135. UI SDK docs_core_llms.txt:2043 "ui-sdk hasn't reached 1.0 yet".
findings.fix: Rewrite A-16 point 2 to quote principle 6 and budget.md:97 and ask the CEO for a named entry on the exception list. Change the default to the more reversible one: UI SDK is used in clay and EXPLORE items only, and no brick component depends on it until the CEO approves the exception. In D-013, replace the principle line with a statement that the decision is an exception to principle 6, softened by the pin and the wrapper.

findings.where: D-013 point 2 "Date picker and calendar for appointment booking; select and combobox; dialog and popover; toast; and the chat helpers"
findings.problem: Q1, Q2. Every part in this list is outside the founding set. The charter says each arrives as an EXPLORE item, promotion is the steward's decision, at most three are active and one is new per slice. D-013 records the list as a lead decision and A-16 does not put it among the CEO's items. The same parts measure 38 to 68 kilobytes each against a 5 kilobyte per-component row that A-16 says "is not changed"; A-16 raises the budget only for the four checkout parts.
findings.evidence: charter/operating-model.md:64 "Adding a new part, variant, token or option outside the founding set. Each arrives as an EXPLORE item, so this is always a promotion | ... | Steward". DECISIONS.md:52 (A-04 row 13) "With no steward, the system can grow only by the founding set". charter/README.md:33 "A work item the lead adds later does not enlarge the founding set." charter/budget.md:134-135 "at most three active items; at most one new item per pilot, or per slice while no pilot is running". charter/budget.md:152 "At most 5 kilobytes per component, 15 for the slice"; budget.md:96 "Budgets never exceeded". notes/sources/raw/2026-11-14-ui-sdk-size.txt: "select ... 67639", "date-picker ... 67954", "dialog ... 51133", "popover ... 46961", "toast ... 44717", "calendar ... 37881".
findings.fix: Reword point 2 as a candidate list, not a decision: each part enters as an EXPLORE item under the cap of three, promotion is the steward's, and none can enter brick under the current per-component JavaScript row. Add both to A-16 as a fourth item for the CEO, with the measured sizes.

findings.where: D-013 "What does not change: the core tasks of the checkout slice need no JavaScript (charter/budget.md) ... UI SDK's default stylesheet is never loaded"
findings.problem: Q4. Two gaps. (a) The charter's no-script rule covers every slice, not only checkout. A UI SDK date picker in the booking slice would sit in a core task, and the facts file says its behaviours need JavaScript, so the sentence quietly narrows a budget row. For checkout it holds only if every UI SDK-backed part ships native fallback markup, which is on component pages nobody read. (b) UI SDK injects a second stylesheet of its own whose contents were not read; the sentence mentions only web.css.
findings.evidence: charter/budget.md:151 "JavaScript needed to read the page and complete the core tasks | None. The page works by sending the form to a server". charter/principles.md:46 "Every core task of a slice can be completed ... inside the performance budgets". notes/sources/2026-11-14-ui-sdk.md:39 "Its behaviours need JavaScript ... Our core tasks must work with none." and :41 "It injects a small stylesheet of its own ... Its contents were not read." UI SDK docs_web-components_llms.txt:1044 "For a control that must submit before upgrade, include a native input or select using the fallback markup shown on its component page." notes/sources/2026-11-14-ui-sdk.md:12 "What was not read: the per-component pages".
findings.fix: Write: "the core tasks of every slice need no JavaScript; a UI SDK-backed part ships native fallback markup and is tested with script off; UI SDK's web.css is never loaded, and its injected behavioural stylesheet is read and checked against the token and browser-feature lints before any part uses it."

findings.where: D-013 point 2 "It is the behaviour layer where plain HTML is not enough ... select and combobox; dialog and popover; toast"
findings.problem: Q1. The list includes behaviours that the lead's own survey and D-008 say the platform already provides (dialog, select), and one the checkout spec rules out (a message that dismisses itself). Principle 6 puts a web standard before a library.
findings.evidence: charter/principles.md:135 "a web standard before a library". UI SDK docs_web-components_llms.txt:1349 "Toast ... Show notifications with actions, timed dismissal".

findings.where: Item 3.5 "Sonnet or Haiku measures; Fable decides | next | Decides DECISIONS.md A-16, point 1"
findings.problem: Q8. Item 3.5 cannot decide A-16 point 1. If UI SDK were in field and button at Gate 3, the one-time reset to "measured value plus a fifth" would absorb it without the CEO. findings.where: D-013 "Reason: It is the only library found that renders one behaviour definition in five frameworks and brings no look of its own"
findings.problem: Q5, Q7. The survey looked at three behaviour libraries, two of them React-only, so "the only library found" is true of a search of three and reads as much stronger. The decision's main reason is uniqueness, and no search for multi-framework unstyled libraries was run. (From the reviewer's own knowledge, not checked in this run: Zag.js and Ark UI are candidates of that kind and should be looked at.)
findings.evidence: notes/survey/behaviour-and-distribution.md headings at :4 "Radix UI Primitives", :10 "React Aria (Adobe)", :16 "UI SDK (vercel-labs/ui)"; :66 "the only multi-framework, agent-oriented option found". charter/survey.md:108 names the same three. `grep -rn "Zag\|Ark UI\|Headless UI" notes charter` returns nothing.
findings.fix: Write: "Of the three behaviour libraries surveyed (Radix, React Aria, UI SDK) it is the only one that is not tied to React. No wider search was made." Add a short survey of stable multi-framework unstyled libraries before any UI SDK part enters brick.

findings.problem: Q3, Q4. No written convention conflicts with data-slot: item 3.1 is still "next". The problems are elsewhere. findings.where: Section "What we take from them now" (the 17 rows)
findings.problem: (g) Four practices in the skills that bear directly on this system are not taken and not mentioned. The first matters most for an assistant product. (1) Copy rules ship with exemptions for text that must stay verbatim and for strings a person or machine pastes elsewhere. Our writing check bans words such as "just", "valid" and "please" and fails on urgency wording in literal text; without exemptions it will flag drafted messages and quotations, or push someone to rewrite what a person sends. (2) Show the first component family to a person before fanning out, which fits item 3.2 (cost summary first) before 3.3. (3) A fix is written as a check that fails on the current build, which fits build-loop step 6. (4) A surface that writes data is checked by request-body equality, which fits the budget row that the amount the test server receives equals the total shown. The reader listed all four.
